text:
In April 2023, most of us spoke as one. Thirty of us warned of the "default on america"; twenty-nine named the "default on america act"; twenty-three of us called it "the default on america act." The bill gave us our script, and we read from it on a single day, April 26, when nearly all of these phrases peaked at once.

Beneath the title we itemized the stakes. Twenty-two of us cited "social security payments"; twenty-one added "social security payments for" whom. Twenty-one of us said the act would make "college more expensive for" someone. Twenty-one invoked "veterans affairs health." Twenty-one warned we would "default on our debt."

We converged inside a day, on one date, around one bill, in the same order of concerns. That is what the record shows of us this month: a coordinated recitation, arriving together and dispersing together.
